Question B-006-005-005.

Why the correct answer is right: High SWR increases feedline loss because reflected power travels through the lossy line as well as forward power.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Increased transmission line loss": Correct. High SWR increases feedline loss because reflected power travels through the lossy line as well as forward power.
- sourceIndex 1: "Increased receive noise level": Those can occur in some stations, but the main high-SWR penalty is extra line loss.
- sourceIndex 2: "Increased transmission line radiation": Small coax at high frequency mainly causes excessive attenuation; heating can result, but loss is the primary adverse consequence.
- sourceIndex 3: "Increased common-mode current": Those can occur in some stations, but the main high-SWR penalty is extra line loss.
